To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the SCT education programme was not effective in enhancing the effects of exercise on secondary outcomes.

1) there are no statistically significant differences for the secondary outcomes between groups, however, there are improvements in fatigue, strength and physical activity that are sustained at 3 months and 6 months post intervention in both groups; 2) in the SCT group only, there are improvements at 3 and six months follow up in cognition, anxiety and depression, physical impact of MS and self efficacy that are maintained above baseline.

exercising at the minimum guideline based exercise amount has a positive impact on fatigue, strength, physical impact of MS, cognition, anxiety and depression and this effect is sustained at 6 month followup.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the exercise intervention combined with SCT education is a feasible, acceptable and effective intervention for people with MS.
the minimum recommendations of the MS exercise guidelines are beneficial for fatigue, strength and physical activity.
exercise has a positive effect and that the addition of SCT education may enhance some of those benefits.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the exercise guidelines for people living with MS have a positive impact.

the exercise guidelines are effective in improving fatigue, strength and physical activity and that the SCT program is effective in improving anxiety, depression, physical impact of MS, cognition and physical activity.
exercising at the minimum guidelines of 30 minutes twice a week can be beneficial for people with MS.
